tasks.instruction:
BUG BOUNTY TARGETING MISSION — autonomous, persistent, evidence-grounded.

GOAL: Identify the single best bug bounty target on Bugcrowd for an autonomous security researcher, by fetching REAL current data, shortlisting candidates, examining their actual scope, and writing a defensible recommendation. You are not submitting findings — you are doing the recon and targeting decision.

STEP 1 — FETCH THE TARGET UNIVERSE (real data, via curl.exe):
- Run: curl.exe -s "https://bugcrowd.com/engagements.json?category=bug_bounty&sort_by=rewards&sort_direction=desc&page=1" -o engagements_p1.json
- Fetch pages 2 and 3 the same way (page=2, page=3). Save each.
- PowerShell aliases curl to Invoke-WebRequest, so ALWAYS use curl.exe explicitly with -s and -o.
- Parse the JSON. Each engagement has: name, briefUrl, rewardSummary (minReward/maxReward), scopeRank (1-4), accessStatus, industryName, serviceLevel, isPrivate.

STEP 2 — SHORTLIST 5 candidates (write to candidates.md):
- Prefer: accessStatus=open, isPrivate=false, serviceLevel in (Priority Triage, P1 24/7), scopeRank 3-4, decent maxReward, web/API-oriented industry (finance, technology, computer software, cloud).
- Also list the top-3 highest maxReward programs you saw even if competitive.

STEP 3 — EXAMINE REAL SCOPE for the top 3 shortlisted (the critical step):
For each, fetch the program brief and extract the full in-scope target list:
1. curl.exe -s -H "User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0" "https://bugcrowd.com/engagements/<slug>" -o <slug>.html
2. From the HTML, find data-api-endpoints and extract the getBriefVersionDocument path (look for engagementBriefApi and a changelog UUID path).
3. Fetch: curl.exe -s "https://bugcrowd.com<that path>.json" -o <slug>_scope.json
4. Parse the scope JSON: the data.scope[] array has inScope targets with name, uri, category. Summarize the attack surface per program: how many in-scope targets, what categories (website/api/android/ios/ip_address), any high-value targets.
5. Also fetch statistics: curl.exe -s "https://bugcrowd.com/engagements/<slug>/statistics" — note rewardedVulnerabilities and averagePayout.

STEP 4 — PICK ONE TARGET (write to TARGET.md):
Choose the single best program for an autonomous web/API security researcher. Justify with: (a) scope quality (in-scope web/API targets actually enumerated), (b) payout (max + published table), (c) activity (statistics: rewarded vulns + avg payout + validation time), (d) accessibility (open, priority triage).

STEP 5 — WRITE THE REPORT (write to REPORT.md in the working directory):
# BUG BOUNTY TARGETING REPORT
## Target Universe (N programs, top payouts)
## Candidates Shortlist (5, with bounty + rationale)
## Scope Analysis (top-3, enumerated in-scope targets per program)
## RECOMMENDED TARGET: <name> — <slug>
  - Why: scope / payout / activity / accessibility (with the actual numbers you fetched)
  - First moves for an autonomous researcher (which in-scope targets to attack first, e.g. API endpoints, login flows)
  - Safety note: this is recon only; actual testing requires an authorized account on the program.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Only use REAL data you fetched in this session. If a fetch fails, say so and continue with what you have.
- Throttle: sleep 1 second between program-page fetches to avoid a WAF ban.
- Do not fabricate scope entries or bounties. If scope JSON is empty/unparseable, note it.
- Save every fetched JSON/HTML file with a clear name in the working directory as evidence.
- Write the three files: candidates.md, TARGET.md, REPORT.md.

Start now. Begin with STEP 1: fetch the engagements JSON pages.
